modules.name: Vista audit and node contract
modules.design_question: Which Vista parts become the View-and-Warn node, and what typed ports does it expose to the rest of the platform?
modules.method: Vista v09.16 is one WebGL2 page: explorer.js (218 KB, about 160 functions, one global state), report.js, pdf.js, six self-test scripts. Flow: Site (point, replaced buildings, drawn boundary), Build (stacked blocks or a rhino3dm .3dm/.obj import checked by part bounding boxes), View (origin = open-data polygon apex, eye 1.6 m over SRTM terrain; highest modelled roof; drag aim), Output (polygon-clip plan overlap, flat user study ceiling, one PDF page per overlapping cone). Plan: keep the geometry kernels, result precedence, no-compliance wording guards, fixtures F1-F3, hash state, PDF writer and cone-fit camera rule; split explorer.js into assets, picking, camera and ui modules; replace the global state and the /api/check shim with typed functions; run checks in a Worker; port self-tests to a headless runner. Replace the 38.7 MB triangle context, apex-only origins, flat ceiling, bounding-box checks and Form Studio's duplicate cone copy. Every output carries units, CRS, vertical datum, dataset versions and an estimate flag; a node refuses inputs that lack a datum.
inputs: ConeSet: per view id, origin lat/lon/z with quality level, boundary azimuths, plan polygon, limit parameters with tier
ContextTiles: LOD1 buildings with height source
DesignMassing: placed triangle meshes, layers, units, datum
ViewpointSet: protected origins, rooftop picks, user points
outputs: ViolationReport per cone: exceedance, uncertainty, worst point, clause ids, estimate flag
ViewRender: existing and proposed images with overlays
SkylineProfile: elevation angle against azimuth
PdfReport
Provenance: dataset versions, hashes, assumptions

modules.name: Protected-viewpoint camera rig
modules.design_question: How do we render the design from each protected origin with correct position, eye height and a field of view matched to the cone?
modules.method: Origin: use City survey coordinates and geodetic elevation when obtained (quality Q2); otherwise the polygon apex (Vista; 16 distinct apexes match the 16 origin points; the four QE apexes agree within 0.33 m) as Q0, labelled estimated. Eye z = ground z + eye height (default 1.6 m, editable; City value not found). Ground z comes from the DTM sampler; pier and bridge views (G1, G2, E) may need a structure offset (Vista falls back to water level on piers). Heading = bisector of the two boundary azimuths (Vista averages far-vertex directions). Presets: cone-fit, keeping Vista's rule hfov = clamp(1.5 x spread + 8, 24, 100 deg), pitch near the lower-boundary angle (City 9.1 sheet implies 2.05-2.12 deg) plus margin; standard 39.6 deg (50 mm equivalent, as cited from UK TGN 06/19). Overlay the two vertical boundaries, the estimated lower-boundary line and an origin-quality badge. Render camera-relative to avoid float32 jitter, near 1-2 m, far 8 km. Calibrate each view once against a site photo: landmark azimuth and elevation within 0.3 deg.
inputs: TerrainSampler ground z at the origin
Structure-offset table for piers, decks and seawalls
outputs: ViewRender per cone: existing and proposed, with boundary and limit-line overlays
Camera record: lat, lon, z, eye height, yaw, pitch, fov, origin quality

modules.name: Rooftop and surrounding-building viewpoints
modules.design_question: How do we offer trustworthy views from nearby roofs and rank which ones matter?
modules.method: Vista picks the highest modelled roof triangle (normal Z share at least 0.35), prefers high, broad, central surfaces, lists up to six buildings within 600 m and sets the eye 1.6 m above the roof; roof heights are OSM-derived and unverified. Upgrade: (1) roof z from several sources shown with their spread: LOD1 context (OSM height plus ground), City building-footprints-2009 topelev_m (2009 LiDAR, stale), and a current DSM where available; (2) treat OSM height as excluding antennas and spires; (3) rank candidates by elevation angle to the design top, distance, unobstructed ray (BVH) and whether the roof lies inside any protected-view cone; (4) a grid index replaces whole-city scans; (5) access flag stays unknown unless a public viewing roof is listed; (6) never imply a rooftop is an official viewpoint. Output RooftopViewpoint with source, roof z plus or minus spread and building id. Reuse Vista's rooftop self-test (stable building ids restored from the URL hash).

modules.name: Cone limit estimate and violation warning
modules.design_question: How do we estimate each cone's limit at any point and warn which cone, by how many metres, where, citing the clause and saying it is an estimate?
modules.method: Polygons alone are not enough. The City's own sheet (2004, View 9.1) uses Hx = Dx(Lr-Lv)/Dr - (Lbx-Lv), so the geodetic limit is L = Lv + (Lr-Lv) Dx/Dr, Dx being distance from view point to site. Tiers: T0 flat user ceiling (Vista, kept as what-if); T1 calibrated, fitting Lv and slope per cone from published site-vertex limits in rezoning booklets (three vertices fix a plane), residuals reported; T2 City-supplied origin elevation and reference data. A point is in a cone when its azimuth lies between the two polygon edges at the apex and its distance is within the far extent. Exceedance e = z_top - L(P). Test exactly by clipping every design triangle to the cone polygon and evaluating clipped vertices (curvature error about s l^2/(8D), under 0.02 m for 50 m edges at 1 km). Uncertainty U = sqrt(sigma_Lv^2 + (Dx sigma_s)^2 + sigma_grade^2 + sigma_datum^2). Per cone report max e plus or minus U, the point (x, y, z, lat/lon, element id), area above, headroom, tier and datum; states: outside, clear, within uncertainty, above. Always print estimate, cite clause 3.1.1 (p.6), list 3.1.2-3.1.5, 3.3 and 3.4 as human review.

Reference table of published site limits for calibration
outputs: ViolationReport per cone: e, U, worst point, area above, headroom, tier, clause ids, wording

modules.name: Skyline comparison and PDF report
modules.design_question: How do we show what the design changes in the existing view and export it as evidence?
modules.method: Render Existing and Proposed from one camera with a wipe slider (Vista puts both in PDF pages but toggles on screen). Add a skyline profile: sample azimuth every 0.05-0.1 deg across the cone plus 2 deg each side (112 to 570 rays); per ray take the highest elevation angle among terrain, existing buildings and design (BVH raycast or depth readback). Outputs: three angle arrays, skyline area added (deg^2), share of cone width where the design rises above the existing skyline, and margin to the estimated lower-boundary line. Overlap with the view subject (named peaks plus DEM ridge) is roadmap. Keep Vista's report engine (own PDF writer, JPEG images, one page per cone, key plan, section) and add the vector profile chart, violation table with plus or minus U, datum line, tier, estimate stamp and a provenance appendix with dataset dates and hashes. Existing context must share an epoch: current OSM, 2009 LiDAR and the 2022 studio model differ, so print the epoch on each image. Add alt text, non-colour cues (WCAG 1.4.1) and a live status region (WCAG 4.1.3).

PdfReport: one page per overlapping cone plus summary, clauses and sources

modules.name: Design ingest and georeferencing
modules.design_question: How do .3dm, OBJ and IFC models become a placed, mesh-level DesignMassing with an explicit datum?
modules.method: Vista reads .3dm in the browser with rhino3dm (WebAssembly, MIT): meshes, extrusions and brep render meshes, a unit table (mm to yards), caps of 80 MB and 2 M triangles; OBJ is parsed locally; placement puts the model's bounding-box base on the terrain at the site; the cone check uses one bounding box per part, which can overestimate. New contract DesignMassing {parts[id, layer, positions Float32, indices Uint32], units, source SHA-256, placement{anchor lat/lon, rotation, base z, datum}}. Placement modes: on site (Vista); as-modelled coordinates with declared EPSG and datum; or base elevation from the sampler with its sigma shown. Layers named mechanical, antenna or mast are flagged as appurtenances, which the quoted clause 3.1.1 includes. IFC through web-ifc; breps without render meshes are reported, never silently dropped. Test: the triangle check equals the bounding-box check on boxes and is lower on a stepped tower. Everything stays on the device; nothing is uploaded.

modules.name: Student-laptop performance and storage budget
modules.design_question: What size and compute budget keeps the node usable on a student laptop and on GitHub Pages?
modules.method: Baseline from the files: Vista's generated pack is 38.7 MB, 1.09 M building triangles, and roof, terrain and pick queries scan triangles linearly. At GitHub Pages' soft 100 GB per month, 38.7 MB per cold load allows about 2,600 loads; 3 MB allows about 33,000. Targets: under 5 MB to first interaction, under 20 MB total, 30 fps on integrated graphics, under 500 MB tab memory. Moves: (1) LOD1 int16 rings like the Program Value Visualizer pack (about 50 B per building against 982 B in Vista meshes), 500 m tiles, LOD2 only within 300 m of the design; (2) heightfield sampler instead of triangle scans; (3) BVH for picking and skyline rays; (4) cone parameters as JSON, not rasters (24 cones, 31.8 km2 summed plan area; a 5 m raster would be 1.27 M cells); (5) check and PDF in Workers; (6) service-worker cache; (7) 2D profile fallback without WebGL. Verify on three laptop classes with a fixed benchmark scene.

outputs: Size and timing report per release

modules.name: AI assistance boundaries and verification gates
modules.design_question: What can GPT-6 Astra and Claude do for this node, and where must survey data and people decide?
modules.method: Allowed, always with a human or deterministic check: code, tests and refactoring of Vista modules; data-cleaning scripts; reading PDFs and figures (rezoning booklets, council reports) into candidate table rows; review of one model's code or text by the other; UI copy and plain-language explanations written from a ViolationReport JSON; fixture generation. Not allowed as a source: terrain, building heights, coordinates, origin elevations, cone parameters or clause text. A 2025 study of two LLMs found coordinate offsets and underestimated elevations, and Claude's documentation calls coordinate outputs approximate. Extraction gate: each model-read number is stored with its page, then must pass (a) recomputation by the City formula where possible, (b) a second-model read, (c) a human check against the page; failures never enter ConeSet. Live data must be fetched, not recalled: Astra's cutoff is 30 Apr 2026, the Guidelines were amended 4 Feb 2026 and open data refreshed 19 Oct 2026. Treat fetched PDFs and pages as data, not instructions. Check Buildner's AI policy before using AI imagery in an entry.
outputs: Extracted rows with page number and model id
Reviewed code and test cases
Plain-language warning text tied to computed numbers

sources.title: Vista README (release v09.16)
sources.extract: Plan overlap only; open-data cones have no heights; origins estimated from polygons; SRTM 60 m; OSM heights unverified; Shangri-La example overlaps only 3.2.1.

sources.title: Vista data files: viewcones.json, guideline.json, context.json, fixtures.json
sources.extract: 24 cones, 16 distinct apexes, height boundary marked unknown; guideline clauses with pages; context built from OSM-derived heights; fixtures F1-F3 expected results.

sources.title: Vista explorer source (explorer.js, browser-check.js, proposal-geometry.js, report.js, pdf.js, self-tests)
sources.extract: 218 KB explorer.js with global state; linear ray scans; bounding-box part check; cone pages use hfov = clamp(1.5 x spread + 8, 24, 100); six self-test scripts.

sources.title: Vista generated manifests and release-manifest.json
sources.extract: Unified pack 38.7 MB; 1.09 M building triangles; SRTM EGM96 60 m terrain; extension from current OSM; caveat: visual context only.

sources.title: Program Value Visualizer basemap README and core/basemap.js
sources.extract: int16 0.25 m rings; 5,247 buildings in about 261 KB; heights in decimetres; neighbourRoofs query; ODbL attribution; no view-cone data.

sources.title: Form Studio README, scene.js, vancouver-map.js
sources.extract: Three.js plus Leaflet; plan-only view cones from a second copy of cone data; competition model omitted from the public copy; City parcel lookup.

sources.title: Public Views Guidelines (approved 2024-07-10, amended 2026-02-04)
sources.extract: Not opened (HTTP 403). Via Vista: s.2 p.3 defines origin, two vertical boundaries and a lower boundary setting maximum geodetic height; clause 3.1.1 p.6 says no part, including appurtenances, encroaches.

sources.title: View cones dataset metadata (Explore API)
sources.extract: Fields object_id, view_number, view_cone_name, description, url, shape_length, shapre_area, geom, geo_point_2d; 24 Polygon records; OGL-Vancouver; modified 2026-10-19; no height fields.

sources.title: View cones records (live geometry)
sources.extract: All 24 live polygons match Vista's snapshot vertex for vertex at 7 decimals (compared 2026-10-21); view 28 has five vertices, the rest three.

sources.title: Campbell, Vancouver's Views presentation (slides 20-23, 32), December 2004
sources.publisher: City of Vancouver (hosted by URISA BC)
sources.extract: Height formula Hx = Dx(Lr-Lv)/Dr - (Lbx-Lv); View 9.1 sheet in feet with viewpoint 205 ft, reference 485 or 495 ft, 7,818 ft; all six rows recomputed exactly.

sources.title: LTSA Circular Letter 465C: Official Vertical Datum for Legal Surveys in BC (amended 2026-04-01)
sources.extract: CGVD28 remains official for BC legal surveys; HTGVRDBC00 for Metro Vancouver; CGVD2013 in GeoNetBC not for legal use; Land Title Act ties geodetic elevation to approved sources.

sources.title: Height Modernization 2013: A New Canadian Vertical Datum (slides 7 and 9)
sources.publisher: NRCan material hosted by Service New Brunswick
sources.extract: Preliminary table: Vancouver +15 cm (CGVD2013 minus CGVD28); national range -65 to +55 cm; the difference matters for precise regional heights.

sources.title: Building footprints 2009 (Explore API)
sources.extract: 124,181 records from 2009 LiDAR; fields topelev_m, baseelev_m, hgt_agl; modified 2019-05-07; flagged approximate, not updated; tallest record 223.71 m top elevation.

sources.title: Shape Your City: Trout Lake public views update
sources.extract: On 2026-02-04 Council requested further review of the Trout Lake view changes and approved the other guideline updates; no new date given.

sources.title: Shape Your City: Higher Buildings Policy Review
sources.extract: Review in phase 1 (page updated 2026-07-13); protected public views are not being reviewed or updated; Tall Challenge entries due 2026-11-30.

sources.title: Vancouver Tall Challenge page
sources.extract: Registration closes 2026-10-29; Q&A 2026-11-03; submission 2026-11-30; FAQ lists an AI-image policy question (answer unread); site plans and 3D model come with the brief.

sources.title: Vancouver View Cones 2026: 24 Protected Views (secondary)
sources.extract: Secondary: 24 views from 16 origin points; a cone sets maximum geodetic height so site grade changes storeys; zoning governs where stricter; Trout Lake changes referred back.

sources.title: City council reduces view cone protections (secondary)
sources.extract: Secondary: Council updated 11, removed 16, kept 13 views in July 2024; lower portion of the QE Park cone removed; exceptional downtown sites may encroach on retained cones.

sources.title: vancouver-view-corridor-massing (GitHub)
sources.extract: Rhino/Grasshopper study with view J1; ceiling linear in distance from the apex; slope and base elevation are placeholders; true limit depends on site grade and City confirmation; no licence stated.

sources.title: 1040-1080 Barclay: site context drawings and Urban Design Panel minutes (search summary)
sources.extract: Via search summary only: view cone 3.2.1 listed with maximum geodetic elevation 123.201 m; panel minutes say the QE cone crosses the site at 332 ft.

sources.title: 118-150 Robson St and 828 Cambie St application booklet (search summary)
sources.extract: Via search summary only: vertex F at 105.71 m under cone A (Alder Terrace), companion point 105.69 m; only listed geodetic heights definitive; appurtenances included.

sources.title: London View Management Framework SPG, Part 1 (GLA, March 2012)
sources.extract: Assessment points with a 120-degree field; protected vistas have a threshold plane above Ordnance Datum; accurate visual representations accompany assessment; appendix E computes consultation-plane height.

sources.title: Landscape Institute TGN 06/19 as cited in a UK planning document
sources.extract: Via search summary only: 50 mm lens gives about 39.6 deg horizontal field; wider prime lenses when 50 mm cannot capture the view; one consultant used a 1.6 m tripod.

sources.title: GitHub Pages limits
sources.extract: Published site up to 1 GB; repository recommended up to 1 GB; soft bandwidth 100 GB per month; 10 builds per hour soft; 10-minute deploy timeout.

sources.title: Can I use: WebGL2
sources.extract: 97.13% global support; first supported in Chrome 56, Firefox 51, Safari 15, Edge 79.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-6-Astra (OpenAI Developer Community)
sources.extract: Announcement text: 1,050,000-token context, 128,000 max output, cutoff 2026-04-30, $10 input and $50 output per million tokens; modalities not stated; trusted-access cyber rollout.

sources.title: GPT-6 (Wikipedia)
sources.extract: Astra previewed 2026-09-03 and released to paid users 2026-09-04; Sol and Luna 2026-09-22; Instant 2026-10-07; paid version rejects some cybersecurity prompts.

sources.title: Claude API docs: PDF support
sources.extract: 32 MB request; 600 pages (100 if context under 1 M tokens); each page read as text plus image; subject to vision limitations.

sources.title: Claude API docs: Vision limitations
sources.extract: Coordinate and localisation outputs are approximate and need verification; counts approximate; mistakes possible on low-quality or small images.

sources.title: OpenAI docs: PDF file inputs
sources.extract: Text plus page images for vision-capable models; under 50 MB per file and per request; non-PDF files lose embedded charts.

sources.title: Abbasi et al., The World As Large Language Models See It (arXiv 2506.00203)
sources.extract: GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash showed systematic and random geocoding errors and underestimated elevations in Austria; reliability inconsistent; fine-tuning with geographic data suggested.

sources.title: W3C WCAG 2.1 Understanding 1.4.1 Use of Color and 4.1.3 Status Messages
sources.extract: 1.4.1 (level A): colour is not the only visual means of conveying information; 4.1.3 (level AA): status messages are programmatically determinable.

sources.title: HRDEM CanElevation Series (Open Canada)
sources.extract: 1 m or 2 m LiDAR DTM and DSM in the south; CGVD2013; GeoTIFF; Open Government Licence - Canada; modified 2026-05-29; coverage gradual; no accuracy statement.

sources.title: LidarBC (BC Government)
sources.extract: Provincial LiDAR as LAZ plus derived DEMs under Open Government Licence - BC; the page states no vertical datum and no Metro Vancouver coverage.

sources.title: BC height transformations
sources.extract: HTGVRDBC00 covers Metro Vancouver to Langley; converts ellipsoid heights to CGVD28; BYN, Leica, Trimble files; no accuracy statement.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap wiki: Key:height
sources.extract: Building height is the maximum from lowest terrain contact to the top including roof; antennas, spires and rooftop equipment excluded; metres by default.

sources.title: rhino3dm (GitHub)
sources.extract: MIT licence; JavaScript plus WebAssembly build; Vista bundles 8.35.0 (2.67 MB wasm) served from its own origin.

sources.title: web-ifc (GitHub)

sources.title: three-mesh-bvh (GitHub)
sources.extract: MIT; BVH for raycasting three.js meshes; README claims 500 rays against an 80,000-polygon model at 60 fps.

flags.claim: Each cone's polygon geometry is enough to estimate maximum building height at every location.
flags.correction: Polygons give plan extent and apex only; the limit also needs origin geodetic elevation plus reference-point or published site-limit data.
flags.detail: Dataset has no height fields (verified). City method uses Lv, Lr, Dr (2004 sheet). Plan: calibrate from published site limits and ask views@vancouver.ca.

flags.claim: A flat study ceiling is a useful stand-in for the cone lower boundary.
flags.correction: The boundary rises about 2.05-2.12 deg (3.6-3.7 m per 100 m) in the 2004 View 9.1 sheet, so a flat plane drifts about 36 m per km.
flags.detail: Keep the flat ceiling only as a labelled what-if; default to a sloped estimate with uncertainty.

flags.claim: The polygon apex equals the by-law origin point (Vista).
flags.detail: 16 apexes match the 16 origin points and the four QE apexes agree within 0.33 m, but no survey check exists; a search summary says older views lack surveyed coordinates.
No City eye height found; a Council motion reportedly cites a 5 ft 6 in average person (stature 1.68 m, not eye height). Keep editable and labelled.

flags.claim: Vertical datum of the City's geodetic cone heights.
flags.detail: CGVD28 is likely: BC legal surveys use it (LTSA 465C). HRDEM is CGVD2013, SRTM is EGM96; preliminary Vancouver offset +0.15 m. City datum statement not read.

flags.claim: Which Trout Lake geometry (27.1, 27.2) is in force.
flags.detail: Vista's Table 1 extract says amended 2026, but the City says Council requested further review on 2026-02-04. Live polygons equal Vista's September snapshot.
guidelines.vancouver.ca, vancouver.ca, council.vancouver.ca and rezoning.vancouver.ca returned HTTP 403; clause pages come from Vista's guideline.json, rezoning limits from search summaries only.

flags.claim: One planar or conical surface per view describes the City limit.
flags.detail: 2004 slides mention sub-cones, view shadow and a complex QE cone; the QE lower portion was reportedly removed in 2024. Test piecewise multi-reference models.

flags.claim: Vista code and data packs can be reused openly.
flags.detail: None of the four repos has a LICENSE file; the pack derives from a studio-supplied model plus OSM (ODbL); Form Studio omitted the competition model for ownership. Add MIT or Apache; rebuild packs.

flags.claim: Buildner's policy on AI-generated images in entries.
flags.detail: The Tall Challenge FAQ lists the question; the answer was not read. Check before using GPT-6 Astra or any generator for entry imagery.

flags.claim: GPT-6 Astra reads images and PDFs reliably.
flags.detail: Press and OpenAI forum text confirm release (3-4 Sep 2026), 1.05 M context and $10/$50 pricing; image or PDF input is not stated in the sources opened.

flags.claim: Student laptops meet 5 MB, 30 fps and 500 MB targets.
flags.detail: No device survey; the 0.56 s check was measured on one i7-14650HX desktop-class CPU only. Test on three laptop classes.

flags.claim: OSM and 2009 LiDAR roof heights are good enough for rooftop views.
flags.detail: OSM height excludes antennas and spires, but the City counts appurtenances; footprints-2009 is approximate, not updated, datum unstated; 4,800 of 9,897 studio-model heights are type estimates.

flags.claim: SRTM is accurate enough for origin elevations.
flags.detail: No vertical error figure verified; SRTM likely includes canopy and buildings (unverified); origin error reaches the limit up to 1:1. Prefer LiDAR DTM where covered.

Reference-point elevation Lr, distance Dr, sub-cone and view-shadow geometry for each of the 24 views. Same searches; only the 2004 View 9.1 example found.
Whether the lower boundary is a radial cone or a plane in current practice; only the 2004 sheet formula (distance from view point to site) was found.
City eye height used when origins were set; only a 5 ft 6 in average-person reference seen in a search summary.
Vertical datum of City geodetic heights; searched LTSA, BC and NRCan pages; City booklet text not readable.
Survey coordinates for origins of older views; a search summary says some views are described only by words and images.
Which published limits survive the 2024-2026 amendments (QE lower portion, Cambie views, Clinton Park 28, Trout Lake).
Reuse terms for City rezoning booklets and per-view pages; the Open Government Licence - Vancouver text was not found on the portal licence page.
List of accessible public rooftops and their access rules; not searched in depth.
View-subject extents (named peaks) per view for skyline overlap; BCGNIS coordinates and licence unconfirmed.
Student-laptop hardware mix among 2026 entrants; no survey found.
